bull.b: Rapid customer acquisition combined with improving revenue per customer indicates expanding reach and stronger monetization, not merely promotional volume. If these unit economics persist, DraftKings can compound revenue while gaining operating leverage across its digital gaming platform.

Positive operating and free cash flow provides internal funding for product development, market expansion, and customer acquisition despite ongoing GAAP losses. This improves liquidity and gives management more flexibility to pursue growth without relying entirely on external financing.

Vertical integration through an in-house exchange and market-making capabilities can improve economics and increase lifetime-value capture as activity scales. Regulatory approval and participation across multiple exchanges also strengthen DraftKings’ infrastructure and product breadth.

bear.b: A return to net losses and negative EBIT shows that improved margins have not yet translated into durable GAAP profitability. Continued sensitivity to spending levels and operating leverage leaves earnings quality less predictable and could delay sustained self-funded growth.

Higher leverage alongside shrinking equity reduces financial flexibility and makes the balance sheet less resilient if profitability weakens. It can also constrain capital allocation by increasing the importance of cash preservation while DraftKings continues investing in expansion.

The Predictions initiative requires substantial near-term investment before meaningful revenue contribution, creating a material drag on reported EBITDA. Returns depend on successful scaling, customer conversion, and regulatory execution, increasing the risk that capital deployment outpaces monetization.
